name: ISBLANK
description: ISBLANK returns TRUE only when a cell contains absolutely nothing—no value, no formula, and no space.
tldr: Tests whether a cell is truly empty.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The cell reference to test (typically a single cell).

basicExample.explanation: A1 contains nothing, so the function returns TRUE.

advancedExamples.title: A formula returning "" is NOT blank
advancedExamples.description: Show the difference between empty and empty-string
advancedExamples.explanation: Even though A1 displays blank, the formula returned "" which is text, so ISBLANK returns FALSE.

advancedExamples.title: A space is not blank
advancedExamples.scenario: B2 contains a single space character.
advancedExamples.explanation: A space is text, so the cell is not blank.

howItWorks: ISBLANK returns TRUE only when the referenced cell contains no value and no formula—not even a formula that returns an empty string. A formula that returns "" is still considered non-blank, as is a single space or any other character.

howToSteps.name: Pick the cell
howToSteps.text: Select the cell you want to test.

howToSteps.name: Read the result
howToSteps.text: TRUE means truly empty, FALSE means it holds something.

limitations: A formula returning "" is not considered blank.
A single space is text, not blank.
Tests one cell; for ranges wrap it in an array function like SUMPRODUCT.

commonErrors.error: Thinks an empty string is blank

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ISBLANK works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: Does ISBLANK detect a formula that returns ""?
faq.answer: No, only truly empty cells return TRUE; use =A1="" for an empty string.

faq.question: Does a space count as blank?
faq.answer: No, a space is text, so ISBLANK returns FALSE.

faq.question: How do I count blank cells including empty strings?
faq.answer: Use COUNTBLANK, which counts both truly empty cells and cells containing empty text.
